text:
alex: Quick sync — I'm prototyping an escape-hatch header to smooth the v3->v4 cutover. Idea: clients set `X-RW-Compat: v3` (or `v3:strict`) for a short TTL so they keep old behavior while we roll. Thoughts on semantics & risks?

marta: Love the idea. We need to decide whether the header is transient (TTL) or sticky per-tenant. TTL seems safer to me.

samir: Concern: routing and perf. If honor-ing the header triggers a proxy-side translation path, that adds ~1–3ms and extra CPU. For high-QPS tenants that can matter. Do we accept that hit?

alex: Good call. Proposal: header is allowed only when tenant has an opt-in flag enabled. Default off. Header must include `X-RW-Compat-TTL: <seconds>` to prevent long-lived escapes.

marta: Also, we should tag traces and metrics: `compat.header.used=true/false` and emit `compat.header.v3.count` so we can measure adoption and error rates. Add a deprecation code in spans.

samir: Streaming edge-case: translating payloads for streaming endpoints is risky (chunk boundaries, SSE/WS frames). Suggest we disallow the header for `/stream` and `/chatstream` endpoints and return 400 with a migration link.

alex: Agreed. Guard it at the router: reject for streaming routes. For non-stream generation endpoints we do translation at ingress before handing to runtime.

ops-bot: deploybot: rolling deploy of `compat-bridge` v0.1 to staging at 1718754400 :rocket:

marta: We should also enforce an "escape window" policy: the tenant-level opt-in can be enabled only for an active migration window (configurable). If outside the window, header yields 403. We can't let it be a permanent escape hatch.

samir: Implementation sketch: a lightweight `compat-bridge` service in front of the runtime that rewrites request shapes and headers according to tenant rules. Keep a small in-memory cache for mapping rules. Fallback: if translation fails, we either (a) return `X-RW-Compat-Result: rejected` with error, or (b) fallback to v4 behaviour and add `X-RW-Compat-WARN`. Which do we prefer?

alex: Prefer (b) as default for resilience, but make it configurable per-tenant (fail-close vs fail-open). Fail-open with a warning header lets customer traffic keep flowing while we triage.

marta: Add a small example in the RFC and define canonical header semantics. Example: 
```http
POST /v4/generate
X-RW-Compat: v3
X-RW-Compat-TTL: 60
Content-Type: application/json

{ "prompt": "write a haiku" }
```
Response should include `X-RW-Compat-Result: translated|passthrough|rejected` so we can detect when translation was applied.

samir: Also: billing. If we translate payloads (e.g., expand prompts) we must ensure the billing pipeline doesn't double-count tokens or misattribute costs. Add billing integration to the plan.

alex: Noted — I'll add billing and regression tests (prompt->instruction mapping) to the RFC. I'll also propose telemetry keys and dashboards (error rates, translation latency, tokens delta).

marta: One more: security review. Translation rules may touch PII redaction or request metadata — require a short security sign-off for the bridge rules.

alex: Thanks. I'll draft an RFC with: header semantics, tenant opt-in gating, TTL semantics, streaming exclusions, fail-open/fail-close toggle, telemetry & billing notes, and a short prototype plan (compat-bridge + infra deploy). Will create a staging test and open tickets for perf testing.

samir: SGTM. Would like to see a microbenchmark for average added latency and CPU impact per QPS.

alex: Yep. I'll include perf targets (p50 add <2ms at 10k RPS, p95 <7ms) in the RFC. Opening RFC + staging deploy ticket now.

marta: Thanks — this feels like a practical path that avoids long-lived shims while giving customers a controlled escape hatch. :thumbsup:
